findings.title: Double-checked locking is incomplete: no re-check of the cache after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: GetWebAssets reads the cache under RLock, and if empty, acquires the write lock and unconditionally re-reads the manifest without re-checking whether another goroutine already populated the cache in the meantime. Two consequences in non-Dev mode: (1) redundant duplicate file reads on a cold start, and more importantly (2) goroutine A succeeds and caches a valid *dtos.EntryPointAssets; goroutine B, waiting behind A, then re-reads the file and if that read fails transiently, line 69 (`entryPointAssetsCache = result`) overwrites the good cached value with nil and B returns an error — a user-visible failure even though a valid cached result existed. The fix is to re-read `entryPointAssetsCache` after taking the write lock (or before assigning at line 69) and return the cached value if it is now non-nil in non-Dev mode.

findings.title: Write lock is held across file/network I/O, serializing all GetWebAssets callers
findings.body: The deferred-unlocked write lock at lines 48-49 is held while `readWebAssetsFromFile` performs disk I/O (and, if the `cdn` variable is ever set, `readWebAssetsFromCDN` performs an HTTP request via `http.DefaultClient`, which has no timeout — a hang there would block every GetWebAssets caller indefinitely). In Dev mode the cache check is skipped entirely, so every request re-reads the manifest file while holding the write lock, serializing all concurrent requests that touch this path. Computing `result` outside the lock and taking the write lock only to publish the cache assignment would avoid blocking all readers for the duration of the I/O.

findings.title: The mutex guards the cache pointer but not the shared EntryPointAssets struct it returns
findings.body: The fix prevents races on the `entryPointAssetsCache` variable itself, but all callers still receive the same shared `*dtos.EntryPointAssets` instance. Any caller that mutates the returned struct — for example via its `SetContentDeliveryURL` method, which the code itself calls on the result at line 64 — would race with concurrent readers of that same pointer. To fully close the race, the cached value must be treated as immutable after publication (and any mutation, such as SetContentDeliveryURL, must happen before it is stored), or a copy returned per call.
